incidents.victim: Denmark CPR Register (national population registry — ~8.8 million residents)
incidents.vector: Unauthorized access via credentials belonging to a compromised third-party company that held authorized access to the registry.
incidents.impact: Names, home addresses, and 10-digit CPR numbers for virtually the entire Danish population exposed; Danish government minister described the breach as "very serious." Scope of downstream misuse under investigation.

incidents.victim: ATB-Market (Ukraine's largest grocery chain, 1,300+ stores)
incidents.vector: Data theft from customer database; group published sample records on a dark-web leak site and demanded a $400,000 ransom.
incidents.impact: Group claims 7.9 million customer records stolen (names, phone numbers, emails, addresses, password hashes, and over 11 million order records); ATB denies any data compromise; investigation ongoing.

incidents.victim: University of Illinois Chicago (UIC) College of Medicine
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — ransomware (Booba group, likely Frag ransomware rebrand)
incidents.vector: Ransomware attack with concurrent data exfiltration; 344 GB of data stolen before encryption.
incidents.impact: 344 GB of data exfiltrated and ransom demanded; all systems subsequently restored; full scope of exposed records not yet publicly disclosed.

incidents.victim: Bitget (Singapore-based cryptocurrency exchange)
incidents.vector: Compromise of hot wallet infrastructure at the Singapore-based exchange; specific attack vector not yet publicly disclosed.
incidents.impact: $350 million stolen from Bitget hot wallets; one of the largest cryptocurrency exchange thefts of 2026; attribution and full technical details pending.

incidents.victim: DIVD — Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Disclosure
incidents.vector: Suspected autonomous AI agent used to probe and breach internal systems of the non-profit vulnerability disclosure organization.
incidents.impact: Internal DIVD systems compromised; scope of data exposure under investigation; notable as a suspected AI-agent-driven intrusion against a security research organization.

incidents.victim: ATNS — Air Traffic and Navigation Services (South Africa)
incidents.vector: Ransomware deployed across ATNS operational technology (OT) network and weather services infrastructure; insider employee collaboration suspected as a contributing factor.
incidents.impact: Air traffic control and weather services networks disrupted; ATNS manages approximately 6% of global airspace, and the attack threatened air travel across southern Africa and beyond; contained without confirmed mid-air incidents.

incidents.victim: SpetsVuzAvtomatika (Russia — SVR-linked cyber R&D institute)
incidents.vector: Internal document exfiltration from a Russian state-linked cybersecurity research and development organization.
incidents.impact: Internal documents from a research center linked to Russia's SVR foreign intelligence service leaked publicly; content and operational significance under analysis.

incidents.victim: U.S. Department of Defense — DMDC (Defense Manpower Data Center)
incidents.vector: Misconfigured file-sharing server left publicly accessible for approximately nine months (October 2025 through July 2026).
incidents.impact: Personal data for 3.1 million individuals (2.8 million living and 294,000 deceased military personnel) exposed for approximately nine months before discovery; potential foreign intelligence exploitation.

incidents.victim: Organizations using Fortinet FortiMail globally
incidents.vector: Path traversal zero-day in FortiMail's Identity-Based Encryption (IBE) feature; unauthenticated attackers exploit null byte injection to write arbitrary files and achieve remote code execution.
incidents.impact: Active exploitation confirmed before Fortinet's October 2 patch release; indicators of compromise published; organizations should patch immediately or disable the IBE feature as interim mitigation.

incidents.victim: Cryptocurrency users globally (ClearFake campaign)
incidents.vector: ClearFake fake browser-update lure delivers crypto-stealing malware via WebDAV, bypassing traditional file-download security controls on compromised websites.
incidents.impact: Ongoing campaign targeting cryptocurrency wallet holders globally; victims tricked into installing credential-stealing malware via fake browser update prompts.

incidents.victim: Japanese enterprises — Daiwa Securities, Yamato Transport, Dai-ichi Life, Sagawa Express, Ikegami Tsushinki
incidents.vector: Multiple breach vectors across different organizations; Daiwa Securities exposed via a third-party vendor compromise.
incidents.impact: Wave of data breaches hit major Japanese enterprises in September–October 2026; approximately 110,000 Daiwa Securities customers affected; full scope across all named organizations still being assessed.

incidents.victim: Government and policy organizations — Taiwan, India, Philippines, Cambodia
incidents.vector: Custom 'Antino' backdoor malware delivered via spear-phishing targeting government ministries and policy research organizations across four Asian countries.
incidents.impact: Multiple government and policy organizations across Asia compromised; persistent backdoor access established for data collection and ongoing exfiltration; campaign assessed as active.

incidents.victim: Nikkei (Japan's leading financial media organization)
incidents.vector: Two separate intrusions: a Microsoft 365 account compromised and used to relay 9,000 phishing emails to journalistic contacts; and separate unauthorized Google Workspace access running from late July through September.
incidents.impact: Data for 1,646 people exposed via the Workspace breach; 9,000 phishing emails sent to journalists' sources via Nikkei's compromised M365 account, damaging source confidentiality.

incidents.victim: U.S. financial institutions — multiple banks (ATM networks)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — ATM jackpotting (Tren de Aragua, Venezuela-based designated FTO)
incidents.vector: Physical installation of jackpotting malware on U.S. ATM hardware followed by remote activation to force unauthorized cash dispensing; proceeds laundered through cryptocurrency.
incidents.impact: Over $40.7 million stolen across 1,500+ ATM attacks; U.S. Treasury sanctioned 10 network members on September 30, 2026; lead operator (alias "Prometheus") placed on FBI Ten Most Wanted list.

incidents.victim: Global organizations — government, financial services, education, telecom, legal (North America and Europe)
incidents.vector: Zero-day exploitation of Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway appliances (CVE-2026-88771, CVSS 9.5, command injection; CVE-2026-88772, CVSS 9.5, RCE); exploitation began September 3, weeks before disclosure; public PoC available; a related DoS CVE (2026-88779) used to crash appliances and accelerate exploitation.
incidents.impact: Dozens of organizations confirmed compromised across North America and Europe; novel tunneler malware used for credential theft and network reconnaissance; 50,000+ internet-exposed instances globally; Citrix delayed official disclosure by 36 hours after active exploitation was known.

incidents.victim: AT&T and Verizon (100M+ customer records; Snowflake cloud environment)
incidents.attacker: Criminal — convicted hacker (U.S. Army soldier, hacker-for-hire)
incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to AT&T's Snowflake cloud data warehouse; over 100 million customer call records exfiltrated and used to extort AT&T and Verizon with threats to disclose national-security-sensitive content.
incidents.impact: U.S. Army soldier Cameron John Wagenius sentenced to 70 months in federal prison on September 25; breach confirmed at over 100 million AT&T customer records; both carriers made extortion payments.

incidents.victim: FBI — apply.fbijobs.gov (5,000+ FBI agents and applicants)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of CVE-2026-35273, a zero-day in Oracle PeopleSoft, to breach the FBI's job application portal; attack framed as retaliation for an FBI public advisory targeting the group.
incidents.impact: SSNs, psychiatric evaluation files, and sensitive personal data on over 5,000 FBI agents and applicants stolen; site defaced; group demanded FBI retract a public advisory rather than a monetary ransom.

incidents.victim: Dozens of organizations using Oracle PeopleSoft (multiple sectors)
incidents.vector: Mass exploitation of CVE-2026-35273, a zero-day in Oracle PeopleSoft; Mandiant/GTIG confirmed widespread campaign scope across dozens of organizations spanning multiple industries.
incidents.impact: Dozens of organizations breached; full data exposure scope still being assessed by incident responders; represents the broadest known exploitation campaign against PeopleSoft.

incidents.victim: Odido (Netherlands largest mobile operator, 6.2 million customers)
incidents.vector: Data breach of Odido customer database, attributed to ShinyHunters during the same campaign period as their other major intrusions.
incidents.impact: 6.2 million Odido customers' personal data stolen and published on the group's leak site.

incidents.victim: Organizations using Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC)
incidents.vector: Active exploitation of a vulnerability in Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center; technical specifics limited in available reporting.
incidents.impact: Active in-the-wild exploitation confirmed; compromised FMC instances grant attackers administrative control over managed firewalls and network-wide visibility.

incidents.victim: Asian government entities and media organizations
incidents.vector: Three-zero-day exploit chain: two Chromium RCE vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-85046, CVE-2026-87491) chained with a Windows ALPC privilege-escalation zero-day (CVE-2026-85880); victims lured via phishing impersonating the Center for American Progress and China Digital Times; novel CLEANGULP malware deployed.
incidents.impact: Asian government entities and media organizations compromised before patches were available; exploit kit shared across multiple Chinese state espionage groups indicating coordinated development; full campaign scope assessed as broader than confirmed victims.

incidents.victim: Healthcare providers — Medyc and MyDr (Poland)
incidents.vector: Ransomware and data theft attacks targeting Polish healthcare platforms over a two-month period.
incidents.impact: 5 million+ patient records stolen from Medyc; separate attack on MyDr platform stole 19 million records in August 2026; among the largest healthcare data breaches in European history.

incidents.victim: Unnamed AI service provider (API infrastructure)
incidents.vector: Theft of AI service API keys used to consume $600,000 in model inference credits over three weeks before detection.
incidents.impact: Approximately $600,000 in AI model usage costs fraudulently incurred; highlights the emerging threat of API credential theft targeting AI platforms and the financial exposure from stolen model access.

incidents.victim: U.S. think tanks, universities, and law firms (AI policy researchers)
incidents.vector: Spear-phishing impersonating a former White House OSTP science adviser; used a Frameless Browser-in-the-Browser (BitB) adversary-in-the-middle tool to bypass MFA and harvest authenticated session tokens; a separate February 2026 campaign impersonated an Anthropic employee targeting the same community.
incidents.impact: AI policy experts at U.S. think tanks, universities, and law firms targeted; MFA bypassed and session credentials harvested; assessed as intelligence collection against U.S. AI policy positions.

incidents.victim: Fideuram — Intesa Sanpaolo Private Banking (Italy)
incidents.vector: AI-generated deepfake audio and video used to impersonate Intesa Sanpaolo CEO Carlo Messina in a fraudulent wire transfer authorization to Fideuram executives.
incidents.impact: €95 million ($108 million) fraudulently transferred in February 2026; €36 million remained unrecovered as of reporting; demonstrates the viability of AI voice and video cloning for high-value corporate fraud.
